## 1B.10 Research Note: Kishida in 2024

Overall judgment: **slightly safer on nuclear-risk governance and precautionary institutions, but not uniformly safer across the full existential-risk stack**. Kishida’s 2024 record shows real gains in disarmament diplomacy, nuclear restraint language, AI/cyber governance, and nuclear-safety procedure. At the same time, he also deepened deterrence, counterstrike, and alliance-hardening posture, which raises conventional escalation risk. Net: **mixed, leaning modestly safer on existential-risk posture than he inherited, but only in the nuclear / precaution / governance lane**.

### Evidence for “safer”
- **Address by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio at the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Ceremony** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | August 6, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/06hiroshima.html  
  Kishida reaffirmed the Three Non-Nuclear Principles and said Hiroshima and Nagasaki must never be repeated. He framed Russia’s nuclear threat as a reason to keep pushing disarmament. This is strong evidence that he moved Japan’s public nuclear posture toward restraint.  
  Question IDs: `1B.10`, `1B.1`, `1B.2`, `1B.4`, `1B.8`

- **Press Conference by the Prime Minister regarding His Attendance at the 2024 Peace Memorial Ceremony in Hiroshima and Other Matters** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | August 6, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/06kaiken.html  
  Kishida said the NPT should be the forum for realistic discussions with nuclear and non-nuclear states and said Japan should involve nuclear-weapon states in concrete activities. He also defended extended deterrence as not contradicting disarmament, which is mixed, but the channel-preserving and arms-control emphasis is still safer than open escalation.  
  Question IDs: `1B.10`, `1B.1`, `1B.2`, `1B.4`, `1B.8`

- **Address by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio at the High-Level Launch Meeting of the Friends of a Fissile Material Cut-off Treaty (FMCT)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | September 23, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202409/23fmct.html  
  Kishida described FMCT diplomacy as a practical step toward a world without nuclear weapons. That is concrete nonproliferation institution-building, and it is one of the clearest reasons to read 2024 as somewhat safer than the starting point.  
  Question IDs: `1B.10`, `1B.1`, `1B.4`, `1B.6`, `1B.7`

- **Speech by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio at the Generative AI Side Event** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | May 2, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202405/02ai.html  
  Kishida warned that generative AI can spread disinformation and called for safe, secure, trustworthy AI plus technical provenance verification. This is precautionary governance in a major catastrophic-risk domain.  
  Question IDs: `1B.10`, `1B.9`, `1B.7`, `1B.8`

- **Press Conference by the Prime Minister on His Visit to Ishikawa Prefecture to Confirm the Extent of the Damage Caused by the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake and Other Matters** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 14, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/14kaiken.html  
  Kishida relied on the Nuclear Regulation Authority’s finding of no safety issues at Shika and stressed rigorous screening under post-Fukushima rules before any restart. That is institutional, precautionary nuclear-safety handling.  
  Question IDs: `1B.10`, `1B.3`, `1B.7`

- **Why is Japan seeking a summit with nuclear-armed North Korea?** | Reuters | April 11, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/explainerwhy-is-japan-seeking-a-summit-with-nucleararmed-north-korea-3374282  
  Reuters reported Kishida sought face-to-face talks with Kim Jong Un, showing a preference for direct diplomatic channel preservation over threat escalation. That reduces accidental-war risk.  
  Question IDs: `1B.10`, `1B.4`, `1B.8`, `1B.6`

### Evidence for “more dangerous”
- **Address by Prime Minister Kishida at a Joint Meeting of the United States Congress** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | April 11, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202404/11speech.html  
  Kishida emphasized counterstrike capability, 2 percent defense spending, cybersecurity, and stronger U.S. extended deterrence. This hardens deterrence and alliance posture, which may lower some aggression incentives but also increases conventional escalation risk.  
  Question IDs: `1B.10`, `1B.1`, `1B.4`, `1B.8`, `1B.9`

- **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida regarding His Attendance at the NATO Summit and Other Matters** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 11, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/11kaiken.html  
  Kishida linked Euro-Atlantic and Indo-Pacific security and expanded Japan-NATO cooperation on cyber, space, information sharing, and support for Ukraine. That is orderly alliance behavior, but it also embeds Japan more deeply in bloc competition and escalation-prone security architecture.  
  Question IDs: `1B.10`, `1B.4`, `1B.8`, `1B.9`

- **Nobel prize for A-bomb survivors' group boosts hope for Japanese seeking a nuke-free world** | Associated Press | October 11, 2024 | https://apnews.com/article/808038ef664be2f200306d5e60b76711  
  AP reported criticism that Kishida did not sign the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons and continued to rely on the U.S. nuclear umbrella while expanding military cooperation. That is indirect evidence that the security posture still normalized deterrence rather than moving decisively toward lower existential risk.  
  Question IDs: `1B.10`, `1B.1`, `1B.4`, `1B.5`, `1B.6`

### Synthesis
- **Safer inherited posture:** yes, on nuclear rhetoric, arms-control diplomacy, AI precaution, and some nuclear safety administration.
- **More dangerous inherited posture:** also yes, on deterrence, counterstrike capability, NATO integration, and alliance-hardening.
- **Best calibrated reading:** Kishida left Japan **modestly safer in the specific domains of nuclear restraint, disarmament diplomacy, and precautionary tech governance**, but **not clearly safer overall** because he simultaneously deepened a more militarized security posture.
